analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 10.6.26
key_insights: Futures are higher again (Nasdaq +60bps, S&P +40bps in the headline, SPX +25bps and NDX +40bps in the macro section) as Nasdaq continues to break out to new all-time highs.
Global bond yields are easing: US 10Yr -3bps to 5.27%, US 30Yr -3bps to 5.63%, France 10Yr -11bps to 4.74%, Italy -11bps to 4.5%, German 10Yr -3bps to 3.46%. WTI is -2.2% at $87.45.

Marine Le Pen, currently leading polls ahead of next year's French election, proposed a sharp deficit reduction, which helped regional sentiment. Bessent said the US can 'very quickly' bend the US debt curve.
Middle East: reports say Yemen recaptured critical territory from the Houthis near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and Saudi Arabia confirmed its East-West pipeline is flowing at 5.8mbd.

GOOGL agreed to a 20-year deal to buy 890 MW of new nuclear power from Constellation Energy (CEG +6%). Constellation will spend more than $4.3B on the build-out, and the capacity comes onto the PJM grid.

STX and WDC are each -2% on competition concerns. Seagate and Toshiba are reportedly competing for TDK's hard-drive magnetic-heads business, a deal worth up to several billion dollars. TDK is the only independent maker of HDD recording heads and supplies Seagate, Toshiba and Western Digital.

SPCX is +2% and breaking out to levels not seen since the early days of the IPO. GS Research published a bullish Q3'26 preview (Sheridan) raising the target to $230 and raising AI segment estimates for capacity, revenue and margins.
GS sees SPCX AI segment estimates as still relatively conservative versus the Street over the next 6-18 months, absent a correction across the broader AI operating landscape.
NVDA is approaching a $6T market cap, up 5 of 6 sessions since the new $150bn buyback announcement, and +1% this morning.
AMD is +2% after CEO Lisa Su predicted 'very high' chip demand for the next few years, said demand is outpacing supply, and reiterated a pledge to invest more than $10B in Taiwan.
PINS named Amazon veteran James Dibbo as CFO, starting Oct. 26, reporting to CEO Bill Ready.

NFLX Q3 2026 earnings preview (Sheridan): shares are down 10% since the 7/16 report versus the S&P 500 +3%, on scrutiny of engagement metrics, which the company now discloses less of, and mixed third-party data.

NFLX debate 1: platform trends anchor a negative narrative that the company has lost share of media consumption, especially in the US. GS thinks the coming report is unlikely to ease this, but a new hit series or film could reverse the stock quickly.

NFLX debate 2: whether more capital is needed, via an IP acquisition or materially higher cash content spend in 2027 and beyond. GS still models cash content expense growing slower than revenue and sees a content mix problem (live and event programming, longer-lived IP) rather than a scale problem.
GS stays very positive on NFLX advertising revenue and platform positioning, citing its digital advertising work.
TSMC earnings preview: reiterate Buy, TP raised to NT$3,300. The 3Q26 analyst meeting is on 15 October. GS forecasts 2026E/2027E USD revenue growth of 42.0%/36.9% YoY, with GM of 67.2%/67.5%.

TSMC CapEx forecasts for 2027E/2028E are raised to US$85bn/US$98bn from US$78bn/US$82bn. GS expects 3Q26E revenue +15.3% QoQ and 4Q26E +11.0% QoQ, with GM edging down to 67.5%/67.3% from 67.7% in 2Q26 on N2 ramp dilution.
Stronger CPU demand driven by agentic AI is cited as a key change for TSMC over the past year, alongside AI GPUs, AI ASICs, networking and server CPUs.

US Autos & Industrial Tech 3Q26 EPS preview: GS expects Auto results and guidance in line to below the Street on average and downgrades GNTX. Industrial Tech consensus estimates are likely moving up, but the bar for the stocks is high.

GS is more positive on Industrial Tech (datacenter capex, cyclical recovery in core industrials, energy and robotics) than on Autos (muted cyclical backdrop). The median coverage stock is down 5% since 2Q26 results and down 4% YTD. Autos are down 5% since earnings and 6% YTD, while Industrial Tech is up 9% since 2Q results and 30% YTD.
Street actions: SWKS upgraded to Buy (B Riley), LSCC initiated at Outperform (William Blair).

Today's calendar: US trade balance 8:30 AM, crude inventories, Eurozone retail sales, $58bn 3yr auction at 1 PM. Fed speakers are Williams, Musalem, Bowman, Schmid and Logan. MRVL, ZS, NOMD and RZLV hold investor days, and AMZN Prime Day runs through 10/7. FOMC minutes come Wednesday 10/7.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and raises the target ahead of the 10/15 analyst meeting on broadening AI GPU, ASIC, networking and server CPU demand, with CapEx forecasts raised.
GS raised its target ahead of Q3'26 earnings and lifted AI segment capacity, revenue and margin forecasts, seeing estimates as still conservative versus the Street.
GS downgraded GNTX in its 3Q26 Autos & Industrial Tech preview, expecting Auto results and guidance in line to below the Street.
Upgraded to Buy by B Riley, listed under Street actions.
Initiated at Outperform by William Blair, listed under Street actions.
GS frames Q3 earnings around engagement and content-spend debates, unlikely to ease the negative narrative, though a hit title could reverse the stock quickly.

sector_views.rationale: Datacenter capex, cyclical recovery in core industrials and secular growth in energy and robotics support fundamentals, although the bar for stocks to move higher is high.
Muted cyclical backdrop, results and guidance expected in line to below the Street, and GS is selective with the stocks.

earnings_insights: SPCX Q3 2026: GS raises AI segment estimates (capacity, revenue, margins) ahead of the report and sees them as relatively conservative versus Street estimates. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.
NFLX Q3 2026 preview: shares are down 10% since the 7/16 report. GS models cash content expense growing slower than revenue and is positive on advertising revenue momentum. No EPS figures are given.

TSMC 3Q26E (forecast, report due at the 10/15 analyst meeting): revenue +15.3% QoQ in USD, GM 67.5% versus 67.7% in 2Q26. 4Q26E revenue +11.0% QoQ, GM 67.3%. 2026E/2027E revenue growth 42.0%/36.9% YoY.
US Autos & Industrial Tech 3Q26 preview: Auto results and guidance expected in line to below the Street. Industrial Tech consensus estimates likely moving up.

Earnings calendar: PENG reports after the close on 10/6, RPM and LW before the open and STZ after the close on 10/6 (in the macro section), Tata Consultancy Services before the open 10/8, DAL before the open 10/9.

tension_points.bull_case: Content success such as new hit series or films could reverse the stock quickly, GS models cash content expense growing slower than revenue, and advertising revenue is gaining momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: Platform trends anchor a narrative that NFLX lost share of media consumption, third-party data is mixed, and investors worry more capital (IP acquisition or higher 2027 content spend) is needed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A new hit TV series or movie in key developed markets could reverse the share price underperformance.
